_about: Numbers cited by the socks5-over-quic-phone-egress kit. Every entry has 'class' = 'public' (a value from an RFC, open-source documentation, or arithmetic on such values; the source says which) or 'illustrative' (a round value invented to teach a relation or a design choice; never a measurement). Design limits (ports, timeouts, stream caps, rate limits) are illustrative with source 'design parameter'. Internal documents are described only generically in SOURCES.md. Load this file; do not retype the numbers.

socks5_domain_max_len.source: RFC 1928 §5: the domain name is prefixed by a one-octet length

socks5_message_sizes.source: my arithmetic from the field layouts in RFC 1928 §3-6 (VER, CMD/REP, RSV, ATYP, address, 2-byte port)

rfc1929_field_max.source: RFC 1929 §2 (ULEN and PLEN are one octet)

quic_amplification_factor.unit: x bytes received from an unvalidated address

quic_stream_id_types.unit: two least-significant bits of the stream ID

quic_first_stream_ids.source: my arithmetic from RFC 9000 §2.1: IDs of one type increase by 4

quic_idle_timeout_min_pto_multiple.source: RFC 9000 §10.1 (effective idle timeout is the minimum of both endpoints' values, and at least three PTOs)

quic_handshake_round_trips.source: RFC 9000 §7 and RFC 9001 §4; RFC 8446 §2 (TLS 1.3 1-RTT); TCP three-way handshake (RFC 9293) adds one; my arithmetic for the sums

quic_crypto_error_base.unit: QUIC transport error code; CRYPTO_ERROR = 0x0100 + TLS alert

rfc9002_initial_window_1200.source: my arithmetic from RFC 9002 §7.2: min(10 x 1200, max(14720, 2 x 1200))

udp_nat_idle_assumption.source: RFC 9308 §3.2 (applications can assume a NAT binding may expire after 30 s of inactivity)

rfc4787_udp_mapping_timer.source: RFC 4787 REQ-5 (many deployed NATs are shorter; that is why RFC 9308 assumes 30 s)

sha256_digest.source: FIPS 180-4; my arithmetic for hex length

token_256bit_hex_chars.source: my arithmetic: 256 bits / 4 bits per hex digit

blocked_ranges_ipv4.source: the cited RFCs; IANA special-purpose address registry (RFC 6890)

value.::ffff:0:0/96: IPv4-mapped: apply the IPv4 rules to the embedded address (RFC 4291 §2.5.5.2)

metadata_address.source: link-local address used by the instance metadata services of several public clouds (provider documentation); inside RFC 3927 169.254.0.0/16

metadata_address_encodings.unit: alternative spellings accepted by inet_aton-style parsers
metadata_address_encodings.source: my arithmetic from metadata_address; the encodings are the classic SSRF filter bypasses listed in the OWASP SSRF Prevention Cheat Sheet

documentation_addresses.source: RFC 5737; RFC 3849 (all example addresses in this kit come from these ranges)

wireguard_timers.source: Donenfeld, 'WireGuard: next generation kernel network tunnel', NDSS 2017, §6.1 (protocol constants)

wireguard_data_overhead.source: Donenfeld 2017 §5.4.6 (type 1 + reserved 3 + receiver index 4 + counter 8 + Poly1305 tag 16); my arithmetic adding IPv4 20 + UDP 8 or IPv6 40 + UDP 8

quic_listen_port_illustrative.unit: UDP port on the cloud instance
quic_listen_port_illustrative.source: design parameter (a common QUIC example port)

socks_listen_port_illustrative.source: design parameter; chosen away from socks5_conventional_port to avoid clashes with other software

front_door_port_range_illustrative.unit: public UDP ports on the anycast front door
front_door_port_range_illustrative.source: design parameter: one static public port per private instance

allowed_ports_illustrative.unit: destination TCP ports allowed by the phone filter
allowed_ports_illustrative.source: design parameter: the HTTP and HTTPS well-known ports only (first release)

keepalive_illustrative.source: design parameter: below udp_nat_idle_assumption and below one third of conn_idle_timeout_illustrative

conn_idle_timeout_illustrative.source: design parameter (QUIC max_idle_timeout on both ends)

relay_idle_timeout_illustrative.unit: s without a byte in either direction

phone_max_incoming_streams_illustrative.source: design parameter: the effective concurrency cap of the whole tunnel

server_max_incoming_streams_illustrative.source: design parameter: the control stream plus one spare

max_established_connections_illustrative.source: design parameter: one device plus headroom for reconnect races

token_bits_illustrative.unit: bits from a cryptographic random source

token_grace_illustrative.source: design parameter: the previous token stays valid this long after a new one is issued

control_payload_timeout_illustrative.unit: s from length prefix to complete payload

control_accept_attempts_illustrative.unit: incoming streams tried before giving up

activity_guard_illustrative.unit: s since the last relayed byte
activity_guard_illustrative.source: design parameter: a device swap is refused while the active tunnel carried traffic this recently

short_lived_threshold_illustrative.source: design parameter: a tunnel that dies sooner than this counts as a failure for backoff

handshake_fail_limit_illustrative.unit: consecutive handshake timeouts before the phone stops retrying

stream_open_timeout_illustrative.source: design parameter: listener waits this long to open a stream to the phone

method_reply_deadline_illustrative.source: design parameter: the phone's method reply is in-memory, so a short deadline detects a dead phone quickly

connect_reply_deadline_illustrative.source: design parameter: must exceed phone_dns_worst_illustrative + phone_connect_timeout_illustrative

phone_dns_worst_illustrative.source: design parameter: worst legitimate resolver time with retries

phone_connect_timeout_illustrative.source: design parameter: phone-side TCP connect timeout

cert_validity_illustrative.source: design parameter: long, because the instance lifetime bounds the key in practice

rtt_cloud_phone_illustrative.source: round round-trip times between a cloud region and a phone

rtt_phone_site_illustrative.source: round RTT from the phone's network to a nearby site

rtt_cloud_site_illustrative.source: round RTT from a cloud region to a site

phone_dns_typical_illustrative.source: round resolver time on the phone

ttfb_model_illustrative.unit: ms to first response byte (server time excluded)
ttfb_model_illustrative.source: my arithmetic in A1 from the rtt_* and phone_dns_typical_illustrative values: method 1 x RTTcp + CONNECT (RTTcp + DNS + RTTps) + TLS 1.3 (RTTcp + RTTps) + HTTP (RTTcp + RTTps); pipelined removes one RTTcp; direct = 3 x RTTcs

latency_target_illustrative.source: design parameter: targets set above the ttfb_model_illustrative floor

latency_test_requests_illustrative.source: design parameter of the end-to-end latency test

cloud_ip_task_failure_illustrative.unit: fraction of web tasks on bot-protected sites that fail or hit a challenge from a cloud IP
cloud_ip_task_failure_illustrative.source: illustrative order of magnitude; the relation taught is 'a large minority, enough to block the product'

residential_proxy_price_illustrative.source: illustrative order of commercial residential-proxy pricing

front_door_fixed_cost_illustrative.unit: USD per month, shared by all instances
front_door_fixed_cost_illustrative.source: illustrative fixed fee of an anycast UDP front door

front_door_per_gb_illustrative.unit: USD per GB processed and transferred

traffic_per_instance_illustrative.source: illustrative proxied traffic of one moderately used agent instance

framing_overhead_illustrative.source: illustrative QUIC framing and keepalive overhead on the phone's data plan

streams_per_page_illustrative.unit: tunnel streams per browser page load
streams_per_page_illustrative.source: illustrative relation: a bypass list for analytics/ads/CDN telemetry cuts tunnel streams by about ten times

heavy_page_concurrency_illustrative.unit: concurrent tunnel streams on a resource-heavy page
heavy_page_concurrency_illustrative.source: illustrative; the relation taught is that one browser page can approach phone_max_incoming_streams_illustrative

native_lib_size_illustrative.unit: MB per ABI, TLS statically linked

fleet_devices_per_instance_illustrative.unit: device QUIC sessions per platform fleet instance

fleet_reconnect_gap_illustrative.unit: s, p99, from fleet-instance loss to device usable again

platform_breakeven_callers_illustrative.source: illustrative: below this the shared platform costs more in raw compute than self-hosting
